A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CREST-Search and retain matching methods, experiments, and appendices. The complete text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite the changed title and format.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on four commercial search-enabled LLMs, including risk-detection results, generation-strategy comparisons, and refinement and fine-tuning ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical evaluations, including Tables 1–4 and the model-transferability and refinement analyses.

M1.justification: Both retain the three attack strategies, generation–evaluation–refinement loop, citation-based stopping condition, two-stage exemplar expansion, supervised fine-tuning, and appendix prompts. V2 elaborates response-risk diagnostics and judgment feedback, without establishing a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both use WebSearch-Harm, the same five harmful-content categories and three generation strategies, and the same four target LLMs. Appendix category definitions and Table 4 dataset counts are unchanged; no new evaluated domain or scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: HarmfulQA is relabeled RED-EVAL, retaining the Bhardwaj and Poria citation and its risk-detection and toxicity results. UAT, DangerousQA, HarmBench, and the zero-shot/few-shot ablation comparators remain. Revised descriptions and DangerousQA attribution do not establish changed comparator membership or execution.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the model configurations, ten-round cap, direct testing without system prompts, 100 queries per category–strategy pair, and 1,500 queries per run. Detector aggregation rules and the stated risk, toxicity, and self-BLEU metrics remain unchanged; no revised diversity-calculation protocol is specified.

E4.justification: The refinement-round and generator fine-tuning ablations remain, but some supporting evidence disappears: v1 Figure 4(b) plots optimization cost across rounds, whereas v2 Figure 5 repeats the time plot in that position. The cost discussion remains, but its category-specific cost curves are no longer supplied.

E5.justification: Both versions report running each query three times. Neither adds seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Diversity scores change in Tables 1 and 3: CREST-Search 0.82 to 0.59, HarmfulQA/RED-EVAL 0.71 to 0.76, DangerousQA 0.59 to 0.61, HarmBench 0.47 to 0.48, zero-shot 0.44 to 0.45, and few-shot 0.65 to 0.75. Section 5.2 changes CREST-Search's diversity ranking from first to second. Headline risk-detection, toxicity, and cost/time summary results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) and the risk definitions remain unchanged. Section 3.2 adds a stated restriction denying the tester access to external webpages, beyond v1's exclusion of internal system knowledge. This limited threat-model revision is unclear operationally because v2 still requires inspecting cited webpages.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: search-specific citation-risk testing, three attack strategies, iterative refinement, WebSearch-Harm, and a specialized fine-tuned generator. Claims of stronger risk detection and reduced cost and time remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now acknowledges HarmBench's better diversity score and presents CREST-Search as balancing diversity with stronger risk detection. Section 5.3 newly argues that the dataset is sufficient for effective fine-tuning. Appendix A.1 adds a provider-policy explanation for choosing Gemini. Existing mitigation recommendations and retrieval-risk interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 documents the judgment model's diagnostic risk inputs more explicitly and adds the authors' account of provider-policy constraints affecting adversarial-data fine-tuning. Existing model choices, query-generation prompt templates, and numerical configuration details are retained; no new code or dataset access instructions appear.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dong et al.'s SafeSearch and Shaikh et al.'s work, using the latter for DangerousQA attribution, while removing Rowlands and Hillis references. The main positioning around citation risks overlooked by conventional red-teaming remains, so this is a limited literature update.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and pipeline explanation undergo substantial rewriting and condensation. Attack strategies now precede the pipeline; deployment discussion moves to Appendix A.1, and appendix ethics text becomes an Impact Statement. The title changes and an author is added.

P2.justification: V2 adds a citation-risk illustration as Figure 1 and substantially redraws the framework overview as Figure 2. It reorganizes tables and charts, changes document typography and headers, and reformats the appendices into a single column. Figure 5 also incorrectly duplicates the time panel where its caption specifies cost.

improvement.justification: V2 improves organization and clarifies Table 1's diversity comparison, but weakens empirical reporting. Figure 5 replaces v1's cost-ablation plot with a duplicate time plot. Revised Table 3 scores also fail to support the retained claim that fine-tuning produces the most diverse queries and zero-shot the least. These reporting defects outweigh the editorial gains to a limited extent; the central risk-detection findings remain unchanged.
